attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: In context, 'not what it used to be' means the partnership has weakened. The normalised wording keeps that without overstating it.

contract.note: The plain reading (weakened, not just changed) is ordinary. Using Q4 2025 and comparing exclusivity and dependence is reasonable, and the rule for changes in both directions is stated in advance.

evidence.note: Jan 2023 baseline: Azure was the exclusive cloud provider. Outside the target period.
Oct 28, 2025 terms: Microsoft loses its compute right of first refusal, non-API products can run on any cloud, and Microsoft may pursue AGI on its own. Exclusivity is clearly reduced.
Same announcement: Microsoft's IP rights extended to 2032 and now cover post-AGI models, Azure API exclusivity kept, and a $250B incremental Azure purchase. Continuing cooperation is strengthened.

reviews.rationale: The Oct 2025 restructuring materially reduced exclusivity and dependence (supports weakening). It also extended IP rights and added a large Azure commitment (strengthening). The contract says material changes in both directions are mixed. The reduced-exclusivity part holds; an unqualified claim of weakening does not.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: In context, 'that deal' is Apple's Siri / foundation-model supplier role, which went to Google. 'OpenAI's to lose' is rhetorical framing and cannot be tested.

contract.note: Reading 'lost' as 'did not secure the role, Google did, and OpenAI was considered' is an ordinary reading. The contract rightly declines to test favourite status or whether OpenAI was rejected against its will.

evidence.note: Joint statement of Jan 12, 2026: Gemini will underpin the next Apple Foundation Models and a personalized Siri.
Contemporary reporting that Apple tested OpenAI's technology before choosing Google, so OpenAI was an alternative considered.

Anonymous source close to OpenAI, relayed second-hand from the FT: OpenAI chose not to pursue the role. A self-serving account that limits any inference of rejection, but it does not negate the support condition.

reviews.rationale: Apple announced that Google's Gemini will power its foundation models and Siri, and reporting shows OpenAI was among the alternatives tested. That meets the support condition. The report that OpenAI walked away is anonymous and self-serving, and under the contract's reading it does not change that OpenAI did not get the role.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Unqualified present-tense claim about the market, with DeepSeek cited as proof. The normalised wording matches it.

contract.note: Reading 'commodity' as broadly substitutable services under real price competition is ordinary. Requiring more than having several capable competitors is fair to the word.

evidence.note: DeepSeek reports R1 is comparable to o1 on a range of tasks. Developer-reported, and it lists its own shortfalls, so it supports only narrow capability parity.
OpenRouter usage data, Jan–Apr 2025 (in period): demand is horizontally differentiated, substitution patterns are limited, and apps use multiple models. Covers one marketplace.
Independent Oct 2025 evaluation shows task-specific strengths and weaknesses across leading open models. Moderate evidence of differentiation.

reviews.rationale: The only usage-based substitution evidence in the packet shows material horizontal differentiation and limited substitution, and an independent late-2025 evaluation shows task-level differences. DeepSeek's self-reported benchmark parity does not establish broad interchangeability. On the contract's terms the commodity claim is contradicted, though the evidence covers only part of the market.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A universal historical claim about OpenAI's net income through the publication date. Reproduced exactly.

contract.note: Net income for the commercial business across its whole history is the ordinary reading of 'never made a profit'. Requiring evidence beyond recent years follows from 'never'.

evidence.note: Reporting dated June 2026 on audited statements: net losses of about $5B in 2024 and about $39B in 2025. Consistent with the claim but covers only two years, so it cannot establish 'never'.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows large net losses for 2024 and 2025 and no evidence of any profitable period. But it has no consolidated results for earlier years, and the entity scope and accounting basis are unresolved. Under the contract, recent losses alone cannot establish 'never', so the evidence does not settle the claim.
